Ms Loretta Pasquale (Physiotherapist)
Templestowe District Medical Clinic,
43 Anderson Street,
Templestowe.

12 January, 2016

Dear Ms Pasquale,

Re: Mr George Chien, 54 years old

Mr Chien has recently undergone right total knee surgery resulting in
limited mobility. I am writing to refer him into your care for suitable
physiotherapy treatment/for rehabilitation.

Upon admission to our hospital on 10 January, Mr Chien, an
osteoarthritis sufferer, was experiencing progressive and severe pain
in his right knee with fluid build up, resulting from/caused by right
total knee surgery. The incision site of his knee has now healed well
and is clean and dry. During his stay he was given appropriate
medication (painkillers and thyroid support) and multiple
supplements. Using a front-wheel walker, he was given assistance
with mobility.

Mr Chien, who still needs supervision for eating, grooming, bathing
and dressing, is to be discharged today with assistance from his
family.

Please note that upon discharge today Mr Chien continues to
experience severe difficulty with mobility, especially in his right leg
and knee. He can walk less than 100 meters using his front-wheel
walker. I am therefore writing to you because he needs your
assistance for acute and comprehensive rehabilitation.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Nurse / Doctor / Physio etc.
